transcript.content: hi, i'm berry. tell me your dream, however it comes back to you.
the kitchen feeling smaller around me, that’s what stuck the most

the kitchen closing in around you. that feeling of a room being less than it should be.

what happened in there?

I was in my grandmother’s kitchen, the one from when I was little, and she was cutting a cake at the table. my uncle Ray was leaning in the doorway smoking. the phone on the wall kept ringing and no one answered it.

a phone ringing and ringing and nobody moves. that would get under my skin.

were you just there watching, or were you part of it?
I was just a kid again, in my red cardigan. I could see it but everything else was black and white

your red cardigan, the only thing with color. like you were the one real thing in that room.

then what happened, when the phone wouldn't stop?
the kitchen kept getting smaller, and I woke up still hearing the phone ringing. the walls were moving in really slowly.

waking up and still hearing it, that’s the kind of thing that lingers all day.

was there anything in that kitchen you kept looking at, something that mattered even if it didn't do anything?
the big round clock on the wall. I kept noticing it but I don’t know why

the clock. just sitting there, not doing much, but you kept going back to it.

do you remember what it looked like?
just an old kitchen clock, big and round. I don’t remember the exact face of it

that's okay, dreams are like that. just the sense of it, big and round and there.

how did it feel when you looked at the clock?
like time was stuck, or like nobody else cared. it felt wrong but I couldn’t say why

time stuck in a room where nobody cares. that would make a kitchen feel wrong all right.

what's the first thing you remember before the phone and the cake?
I don’t remember before that. it just starts with the kitchen already there and the three of us in it

so you're in your grandmother's kitchen, the one from when you were little. she's cutting a cake at the table, and uncle Ray is leaning in the doorway smoking. the phone on the wall keeps ringing and nobody answers it. you're a kid again, in your red cardigan, and everything else is black and white. the kitchen keeps getting smaller, the walls moving in slowly. there's a big round clock on the wall, and you keep noticing it, like time is stuck and nobody else cares, and it feels wrong. then you wake up still hearing the phone.

anything missing?
you got it all right, yeah

it's all there.

want me to draw it for you?
yes, I’d like that

it could go a few ways.

could be a grainy black-and-white film still, the pull of time, with the red only a memory of being alive. or a faded family snapshot, a scene that could be yesterday or thirty years ago, and it's both. or a dark pencil drawing, dark, soft, giving the room a feeling of pressure. or real life with the colour drained out, the kitchen around you muted, and you the only thing in colour. which feels closest, or would you describe your own?
grainy black and white film still with the red only a memory of being alive, that’s closest

so i'll start with you. a small child in the red cardigan, the only thing carrying colour in the grainy black and white, like a memory of being alive. your face i'll leave soft and out of focus, because you never said what you looked like.

anything you'd change, or shall i keep it that way?
keep it that way

ok, i'm sketching you and the grandmother and uncle Ray and the grandmother's kitchen and the cake and the wall phone and the clock now. everything will appear on the right over the next minute or two. once it's there, you can tell me if anything looks wrong.
I see them. the first one with me as a kid looks right. the kitchen feels too open in one of them but most of it’s close. the phone and clock are both there

the first one feels right, good. that open kitchen though, i'll bring the walls in, make it feel smaller like it did in the dream.

give me a moment to adjust it.
that’s better, yeah. it feels more like it did

good. that pressure in the walls, that's the dream.

anything else feel off, or is it all there now?
it’s all there now. looks right

good, that's it then. the whole scene's there.

i'll draw the moments now, in the order they happened, each one carrying on from the last. they'll start showing up on the right as they're ready.
ok, i’ll keep looking as they show up

the first of the five moments is up now, the kitchen with you in it.

does it look the way you remember?
yeah, that looks like it. the red cardigan stands out the way it did

the red cardigan really does, doesn't it. all that grey around it and there you are.

the other moments are still being drawn, they'll show up on the right as they're ready.
i can see a few more now. the one with my grandmother cutting the cake is right. the phone on the wall’s there too

the cake and the phone, both right. that's good.

does that one look like you remember?
the third one i can see, it’s right too. uncle Ray in the doorway feels like how it was even though it’s grainy

that third one feels right for you, uncle Ray in the doorway and all that grain.

three down, two still being drawn. they'll show up on the right as they're ready.
the last one with the kitchen too small, that’s the one that gets me. it looks right, the walls pressing in and the phone still going

the walls pressing in and that phone still going, that one really does get you. it's there.

i also have the moment where you're looking at the clock, and the one where you wake up but still hear the phone. are those how you saw them?
yeah, both look right. the one of me waking up still hearing the phone, it’s weird seeing it but it fits

it's strange seeing it, i know. that moment where the dream follows you into waking.

thanks for sharing this with me. it's all there now, the five of them, in order on the right. look through them whenever you like.
